newsitem.title: ITALY: Two arrested on arson charges in Venice opera fire.
newsitem.headline: Two arrested on arson charges in Venice opera fire.

text.p: Two men were arrested on Thursday on charges of starting a fire that destroyed Venice's historic La Fenice opera house last year, investigating magistrate Gioacchino Termini said.
Judicial sources said Enrico Carella and Massimiliano Marchetti were electricians working on refurbishment of the world-famous theatre when fire broke out on January 29, 1996.
Termini said in an arrest warrant that the two men were held on charges of conspiring to cause the fire and the destruction of La Fenice.
It said their actions put the public at risk and loss of life was only avoided by favourable weather conditions at the time of the blaze and the prompt intervention of police and firefighters.
The arrest warrant said other, as yet unidentified people, may also have been involved in starting the blaze.
Carella and Marchetti both denied the charges.
Investigators at first said fire was probably caused by a short circuit but later their suspicion turned to arson.
Considered an architectural jewel with its gilded and tiered interior, La Fenice held priceless memories as the stage for premieres of some of Italy's most famous operas.
The city has vowed to rebuild the opera house at a cost of at least $100 million.
Last June, Italy's lower house of parliament approved an initial 20 billion lire ($13 million) of government funds for reconstruction.
Music lovers from around the world also have pledged money to rebuild the theatre.
La Fenice, which means The Phoenix in English, first opened in 1792 and was rebuilt after a fire in 1836. ($1=1,534)
